source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 14:1 binds Hebrew 13:23; public 14:2–15 binds Hebrew 14:1–14. All other selected verses bind matching labels.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps rest/burial distinct and names the succeeding son clearly.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. Jehoram his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat rested with his ancestors and was buried beside them in the City of David. His son Jehoram succeeded him as king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. Jehoram his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retains both similar Azariah names and the source's title Israel.
verses.before: He had brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
verses.after: Jehoram's brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat, were Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael, and Shephatiah. All were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He had brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes gifts and cities from the firstborn's royal inheritance.
verses.before: Their father gave them many gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, with fortified cities in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.
verses.after: Their father gave them generous gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, along with fortified cities in Judah. But he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their father gave them many gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, with fortified cities in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.

verses.rationale: Makes consolidation and fratricide explicit without excusing the violence.
verses.before: When Jehoram had risen over the kingdom of his father and strengthened himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword and also some of the officials of Israel.
verses.after: Once Jehoram had taken over his father's kingdom and secured his power, he killed all his brothers with the sword, along with some of Israel's officials.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jehoram had risen over the kingdom of his father and strengthened himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword and also some of the officials of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves accession age and reign length for the repeated closing notice.
verses.before: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.after: Jehoram was thirty-two when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Connects marriage and dynasty while retaining the narrator's moral assessment.
verses.before: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for Ahab’s daughter was his wife. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.after: He followed the ways of Israel's kings, as Ahab's house had done, for he had married Ahab's daughter. He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for Ahab’s daughter was his wife. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the covenant and lamp image rather than reducing them to succession.
verses.before: Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David because of the covenant that he had made with David and because he had said that he would give a lamp to him and to his sons all the days.
verses.after: Yet the LORD was unwilling to destroy David's house because of the covenant he had made with David. He had promised to give a lamp to David and his sons for all time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David because of the covenant that he had made with David and because he had said that he would give a lamp to him and to his sons all the days.

verses.rationale: Renders under Judah's hand as political rule, with Edom's agency intact.
verses.before: In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah and set a king over themselves.
verses.after: During Jehoram's reign, Edom broke free from Judah's rule and set up a king of its own.
verses.tsw_comparator: In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah and set a king over themselves.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult final object without inserting an escape or victory claim.
verses.before: So Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all the chariots with him. He arose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots.
verses.after: Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots. Rising during the night, he struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the chariot commanders.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all the chariots with him. He arose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots.

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator's time perspective and stated reason for Libnah's revolt.
verses.before: So Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled from under his hand at that time because he had abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
verses.after: Edom has remained in revolt against Judah to this day. Libnah also revolted against Jehoram's rule at that time, because he had abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled from under his hand at that time because he had abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors.

verses.rationale: Retains prostitution as the source's sharp religious image, explained in vocabulary.
verses.before: Moreover, he made high places in the mountains of Judah, caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves, and led Judah astray.
verses.after: He also built high places in Judah's hills, led Jerusalem's inhabitants into prostitution, and drove Judah astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, he made high places in the mountains of Judah, caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves, and led Judah astray.

verses.rationale: Preserves Elijah's letter and the two named standards without chronology repair.
verses.before: A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying: “Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
verses.after: A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet: “This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: You have not followed the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or of Asa king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying: “Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

verses.rationale: Keeps divine accusation, religious metaphor, and explicit comparison with murdered brothers.
verses.before: but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel and have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves as the house of Ahab caused Israel to prostitute itself, and you have also killed your brothers, your father’s household, who were better than you—
verses.after: Instead, you have followed the ways of Israel's kings and led Judah and Jerusalem's inhabitants into prostitution, just as Ahab's house did. You have also killed your brothers, members of your father's house who were better than you.
verses.tsw_comparator: but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel and have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves as the house of Ahab caused Israel to prostitute itself, and you have also killed your brothers, your father’s household, who were better than you—

verses.rationale: Preserves all affected groups and property without reducing harm to Jehoram alone.
verses.before: look, the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives, and all your possessions with a great blow.
verses.after: So the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives, and everything you own with a devastating blow.
verses.tsw_comparator: look, the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives, and all your possessions with a great blow.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily horror and duration rather than euphemizing the judgment.
verses.before: And you will have severe sickness with disease of your intestines until your intestines come out because of the sickness, day after day.”
verses.after: You yourself will suffer terribly from a disease in your bowels, until, as the illness goes on day after day, your bowels come out.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And you will have severe sickness with disease of your intestines until your intestines come out because of the sickness, day after day.”

verses.rationale: Preserves divine agency and geographical relationship without modern ethnic substitution.
verses.before: The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians who were beside the Cushites.
verses.after: The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabs who lived beside the Cushites.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians who were beside the Cushites.

verses.rationale: Retains Jehoahaz here and the captivity language without importing later deaths.
verses.before: They came up against Judah, broke into it, and carried away all the possessions found in the king’s house, and also his sons and wives. No son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
verses.after: They invaded Judah, broke into it, and carried off everything they found in the king's palace, as well as his sons and wives. No son was left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came up against Judah, broke into it, and carried away all the possessions found in the king’s house, and also his sons and wives. No son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source's attribution and incurability explicit.
verses.before: After all this the LORD struck him in his intestines with a disease for which there was no healing.
verses.after: After all this, the LORD struck him with an incurable disease in his bowels.
verses.tsw_comparator: After all this the LORD struck him in his intestines with a disease for which there was no healing.

verses.rationale: Retains two years and distinguishes funeral burning from cremation.
verses.before: And it happened after days upon days, at the time of the end of two years, that his intestines came out because of his disease, and he died in severe suffering. His people did not make a burning for him like the burning for his ancestors.
verses.after: Time passed. At the end of two years, his bowels came out because of his illness, and he died in terrible pain. His people made no funeral burning for him as they had for his ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened after days upon days, at the time of the end of two years, that his intestines came out because of his disease, and he died in severe suffering. His people did not make a burning for him like the burning for his ancestors.

verses.rationale: Repeats source figures and preserves the stark unregretted departure and burial exclusion.
verses.before: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He departed without being desired. They buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
verses.after: He was thirty-two when he became king and ruled in Jerusalem for eight years. He departed with no one longing for him. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the royal tombs.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He departed without being desired. They buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

verses.rationale: Keeps older sons' deaths here and identifies the new king despite name variation.
verses.before: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the raiding band that came with the Arabians to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
verses.after: Jerusalem's inhabitants made his youngest son Ahaziah king in his place, because the raiding band that came into the camp with the Arabs had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the raiding band that came with the Arabians to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned forty-two despite chronological difficulty; daughter remains broad kinship wording.
verses.before: Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah daughter of Omri.
verses.after: Ahaziah was forty-two when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for one year. His mother's name was Athaliah, a daughter of Omri.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah daughter of Omri.

verses.rationale: Keeps maternal counsel as the narrator's explanation, not a generalized claim.
verses.before: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in acting wickedly.
verses.after: He too followed the ways of Ahab's house, for his mother counseled him to do wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in acting wickedly.

verses.rationale: Makes plural advisers and the ruinous consequence clear.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD like the house of Ahab, for they were his counselors after the death of his father, to his destruction.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, just as Ahab's house had done. After his father's death, they became his advisers, bringing about his ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD like the house of Ahab, for they were his counselors after the death of his father, to his destruction.

verses.rationale: Retains Jehoram/Joram variation with a short identifying note.
verses.before: He also walked according to their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to battle against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-Gilead. The Arameans struck Joram.
verses.after: Following their advice, he joined Jehoram son of Ahab, king of Israel, in a war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead. The Arameans wounded Joram.
verses.tsw_comparator: He also walked according to their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to battle against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-Gilead. The Arameans struck Joram.

verses.rationale: Preserves Azariah as written here rather than silently replacing it with Ahaziah.
verses.before: He returned to Jezreel to be healed from the wounds they had struck him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel because he was sick.
verses.after: He returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds they had given him at Ramah when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Azariah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to see Jehoram son of Ahab because he was wounded.
verses.tsw_comparator: He returned to Jezreel to be healed from the wounds they had struck him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel because he was sick.

verses.rationale: Retains God's role and son of Nimshi without harmonizing genealogy.
verses.before: But from God came the downfall of Ahaziah by his going to Joram. When he came, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
verses.after: God brought about Ahaziah's downfall through his visit to Joram. When he arrived, he went out with Jehoram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off Ahab's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: But from God came the downfall of Ahaziah by his going to Joram. When he came, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes nephews from brothers and retains the judgment framing.
verses.before: And it happened when Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab that he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers serving Ahaziah, and he killed them.
verses.after: As Jehu was executing judgment on Ahab's house, he found Judah's officials and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers who attended Ahaziah, and he killed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab that he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers serving Ahaziah, and he killed them.

verses.rationale: Makes multi-generation son intelligible; preserves capture location and absence of a strong successor.
verses.before: He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu and put him to death. They buried him, for they said, “He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.” And the house of Ahaziah had no one able to hold the kingdom.
verses.after: He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu and put him to death. They buried him, saying, “He was a descendant of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.” No one in Ahaziah's house had the strength to hold the kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu and put him to death. They buried him, for they said, “He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.” And the house of Ahaziah had no one able to hold the kingdom.

verses.rationale: Retains the sweeping slaughter report, with the rescued exception in the following verse.
verses.before: When Athaliah mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah.
verses.after: When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother, saw that her son was dead, she rose up and destroyed all the royal offspring of Judah's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Athaliah mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah.

verses.rationale: Unfolds dense kinship and pronouns while preserving the woman's decisive rescue.
verses.before: Yet Jehoshabeath daughter of the king took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being put to death and placed him and his nurse in a bedroom. Jehoshabeath daughter of King Jehoram, wife of Jehoiada the priest—for she was the sister of Ahaziah—hid him from Athaliah, so she did not put him to death.
verses.after: But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being killed. She put him and his nurse in a bedroom. Jehoshabeath was King Jehoram's daughter, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, and Ahaziah's sister. She hid Joash from Athaliah so that Athaliah did not kill him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jehoshabeath daughter of the king took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being put to death and placed him and his nurse in a bedroom. Jehoshabeath daughter of King Jehoram, wife of Jehoiada the priest—for she was the sister of Ahaziah—hid him from Athaliah, so she did not put him to death.

verses.rationale: Retains six years and simultaneous rule without relocating the hiding place.
verses.before: He was with them hidden in the house of God six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.after: He remained hidden with them in God's house for six years, while Athaliah ruled the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was with them hidden in the house of God six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps all five commanders and fathers, and retains covenant language.
verses.before: In the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the commanders of hundreds into covenant with him: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
verses.after: In the seventh year, Jehoiada took courage and brought the commanders of hundreds into a covenant with him: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the commanders of hundreds into covenant with him: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Levites and family heads without narrowing Israel to Judah.
verses.before: They went around through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.after: They traveled through Judah and gathered the Levites from all its cities, along with Israel's ancestral family heads. They came to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went around through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Names the speaker supplied by context and keeps the Davidic promise.
verses.before: All the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, “Look, the king’s son will reign, as the LORD spoke concerning the sons of David.
verses.after: The whole assembly made a covenant with the king in God's house. Jehoiada told them, “Here is the king's son! He will reign, as the LORD promised concerning David's sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, “Look, the king’s son shall reign, as the LORD spoke concerning the sons of David.

verses.rationale: Makes the Sabbath shift and first third's task readable across verse labels.
verses.before: “This is the thing that you will do: one third of you priests and Levites who come in on the Sabbath will be gatekeepers;
verses.after: This is what you must do: a third of you priests and Levites coming on duty on the Sabbath must guard the thresholds,
verses.tsw_comparator: “This is the thing that you shall do: one third of you priests and Levites who come in on the Sabbath shall be gatekeepers;

verses.rationale: Preserves the other two stations and the people's separate place.
verses.before: one third will be at the king’s house, and one third at the Foundation Gate, while all the people will be in the courts of the house of the LORD.
verses.after: a third must be at the palace, and a third at the Foundation Gate. All the people must be in the courts of the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: one third shall be at the king’s house, and one third at the Foundation Gate, while all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps restricted sacred access and holiness without equating it with moral superiority.
verses.before: Let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites who minister. They may enter because they are holy, but all the people will keep the charge of the LORD.
verses.after: No one may enter the LORD's house except the priests and the Levites serving there. They may enter because they are holy; all the people must keep the LORD's requirements.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites who minister. They may enter because they are holy, but all the people shall keep the charge of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains death penalty and comprehensive protection, with context defining intrusion.
verses.before: The Levites will surround the king, each man with his weapons in his hand. Whoever enters the house will be put to death. Be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.”
verses.after: The Levites must surround the king, each with his weapon in hand. Anyone who enters the house must be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he comes and goes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Levites shall surround the king, each man with his weapons in his hand. Whoever enters the house shall be put to death. Be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.”

verses.rationale: Explains why both shifts remain without importing the Kings account's personnel.
verses.before: The Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those coming in on the Sabbath with those going out on the Sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest did not dismiss the divisions.
verses.after: The Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each commander took his men, both those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off, for Jehoiada the priest had not dismissed the divisions.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those coming in on the Sabbath with those going out on the Sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest did not dismiss the divisions.

verses.rationale: Retains three weapon categories and their Davidic provenance.
verses.before: Jehoiada the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears, large shields, and small shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of God.
verses.after: Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears, large shields, and small shields that had belonged to King David and were in God's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiada the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears, large shields, and small shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of God.

verses.rationale: Renders right/left spatially for an east-facing sanctuary, retaining altar and king.
verses.before: He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, by the altar and the house, around the king.
verses.after: He stationed all the people, each with his weapon in hand, from the south side of the house to the north side, by the altar and the house, surrounding the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, by the altar and the house, around the king.

verses.rationale: Retains uncertain testimony as a biblical term with a selective note.
verses.before: Then they brought out the king’s son, put the crown upon him and the testimony, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, “Long live the king!”
verses.after: They brought out the king's son, put the crown on him, gave him the testimony, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and cried, “Long live the king!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they brought out the king’s son, put the crown upon him and the testimony, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, “Long live the king!”

verses.rationale: Keeps running and praise rather than substituting a generic celebration.
verses.before: Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, and she came to the people in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king. She went to the people at the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, and she came to the people in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the public scene, pillar ambiguity, and repeated accusation.
verses.before: She looked, and look, the king was standing by his pillar at the entrance, and the commanders and trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with instruments of music leading the praise. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and said, “Treason! Treason!”
verses.after: There she saw the king standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the commanders and trumpeters beside him. All the people of the land were rejoicing and sounding trumpets, while the singers played their instruments and led the praise. Athaliah tore her clothes and shouted, “Treason! Treason!”
verses.tsw_comparator: She looked, and behold, the king was standing by his pillar at the entrance, and the commanders and trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with instruments of music leading the praise. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and said, “Treason! Treason!”

verses.rationale: Keeps both lethal orders and the sacred-location restriction in distinct speech.
verses.before: Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds appointed over the army and said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever follows her will be put to death with the sword.” For the priest said, “You will not put her to death in the house of the LORD.”
verses.after: Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the army and told them, “Take her out between the ranks. Anyone who follows her must be killed with the sword.” For the priest had said, “Do not kill her in the LORD's house.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds appointed over the army and said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever follows her shall be put to death with the sword.” For the priest said, “You shall not put her to death in the house of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserves seizure, route, and execution without adding a trial.
verses.before: So they laid hands on her, and she went to the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king’s house, and they put her to death there.
verses.after: They seized her, and she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate at the palace. There they put her to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they laid hands on her, and she went to the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king’s house, and they put her to death there.

verses.rationale: Retains himself as the first party rather than harmonizing to the LORD.
verses.before: Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be the LORD’s people.
verses.after: Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, that they would be the LORD's people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be the LORD’s people.

verses.rationale: Makes destruction and killing explicit, preserving Mattan's identity.
verses.before: Then all the people went to the house of Baal and tore it down. They broke its altars and images in pieces and killed Mattan priest of Baal before the altars.
verses.after: All the people went to Baal's house and tore it down. They smashed its altars and images and killed Mattan, Baal's priest, in front of the altars.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the people went to the house of Baal and tore it down. They broke its altars and images in pieces and killed Mattan priest of Baal before the altars.

verses.rationale: Follows linked priests/Levites wording while noting another possible coordination.
verses.before: Jehoiada appointed the oversight of the house of the LORD into the hand of the Levitical priests whom David had assigned over the house of the LORD, to offer burnt offerings to the LORD as written in the instruction of Moses, with rejoicing and song according to the order of David.
verses.after: Jehoiada placed the oversight of the LORD's house in the hands of the Levitical priests whom David had assigned to it. They were to offer burnt offerings to the LORD as written in Moses' law, with rejoicing and song according to David's directions.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiada appointed the oversight of the house of the LORD into the hand of the Levitical priests whom David had assigned over the house of the LORD, to offer burnt offerings to the LORD as written in the instruction of Moses, with rejoicing and song according to the order of David.

verses.rationale: Retains comprehensive ritual uncleanness rather than substituting moral worthiness.
verses.before: He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD so that no one unclean in any matter might enter.
verses.after: He stationed gatekeepers at the gates of the LORD's house so that no one unclean in any respect could enter.
verses.tsw_comparator: He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD so that no one unclean in any matter might enter.

verses.rationale: Keeps four participant groups and the procession's descent and destination.
verses.before: He took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land and brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They entered the king’s house through the Upper Gate and seated the king upon the throne of the kingdom.
verses.after: He took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the people's rulers, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the LORD's house. They entered the palace through the Upper Gate and seated the king on the royal throne.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land and brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They entered the king’s house through the Upper Gate and seated the king upon the throne of the kingdom.

verses.rationale: Preserves both communal response and the violent basis of the quiet.
verses.before: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet after Athaliah had been put to death with the sword.
verses.after: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. Athaliah had been put to death with the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet after Athaliah had been put to death with the sword.

verses.rationale: Retains childhood accession, forty-year reign, and maternal origin.
verses.before: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah from Beersheba.
verses.after: Joash was seven when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beer-sheba.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah from Beersheba.

verses.rationale: Keeps the lifetime qualification that structures the following reversal.
verses.before: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
verses.after: Joash did what was right in the LORD's eyes throughout the lifetime of Jehoiada the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the likely referent of him without hiding the two marriages.
verses.before: Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.after: Jehoiada obtained two wives for him, and Joash had sons and daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.

verses.rationale: Retains heart language as purposeful intention, with source segmentation unchanged in binding.
verses.before: After this it was in Joash’s heart to repair the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Some time later, Joash set his heart on restoring the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this it was in Joash’s heart to repair the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves annual collection and the pointed repetition of quickly.
verses.before: He gathered the priests and Levites and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Judah and gather from all Israel silver to repair the house of your God from year to year, and hurry in the matter.” But the Levites did not hurry.
verses.after: He gathered the priests and Levites and told them, “Go out to Judah's cities and collect money from all Israel every year to repair your God's house. See to it quickly.” But the Levites did not act quickly.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gathered the priests and Levites and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Judah and gather from all Israel silver to repair the house of your God from year to year, and hurry in the matter.” But the Levites did not hurry.

verses.rationale: Retains the levy and tent connection without inventing a new tax amount.
verses.before: So the king called Jehoiada the chief and said to him, “Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the levy of Moses servant of the LORD and of the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?
verses.after: The king summoned Jehoiada the chief priest and asked, “Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the levy of Moses, the LORD's servant, and Israel's assembly for the tent of the testimony?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king called Jehoiada the chief and said to him, “Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the levy of Moses servant of the LORD and of the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?

verses.rationale: Keeps sons as agents and the narrator's description of Athaliah.
verses.before: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of God and had even used all the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals.”
verses.after: For the sons of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into God's house and even used all the sacred things from the LORD's house for the Baals.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of God and had even used all the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals.”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes collection chest from covenant ark by context.
verses.before: The king commanded, and they made one chest and put it outside at the gate of the house of the LORD.
verses.after: At the king's command, they made a chest and placed it outside the gate of the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king commanded, and they made one chest and put it outside at the gate of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves Mosaic wilderness connection and the offering's recipient.
verses.before: They made a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the levy that Moses servant of God had laid upon Israel in the wilderness.
verses.after: They issued a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the levy that Moses, God's servant, had imposed on Israel in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the levy that Moses servant of God had laid upon Israel in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Leaves finished without supplying a particular collection target or deadline.
verses.before: All the officials and all the people rejoiced, and they brought and threw into the chest until they had finished.
verses.after: All the officials and all the people were glad to bring their contributions and drop them into the chest until they had finished.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the officials and all the people rejoiced, and they brought and threw into the chest until they had finished.

verses.rationale: Unfolds collection procedure and joint oversight without omitting repetition.
verses.before: And it happened whenever the chest was brought to the king’s officials by the hand of the Levites and they saw that there was much silver, the king’s scribe and the official of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, take it, and return it to its place. Thus they did day by day and gathered silver in abundance.
verses.after: Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king's officers and they saw that it held a large sum, the king's scribe and the chief priest's officer came and emptied it. They carried it back to its place. They did this day after day and collected a great deal of money.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened whenever the chest was brought to the king’s officials by the hand of the Levites and they saw that there was much silver, the king’s scribe and the official of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, take it, and return it to its place. Thus they did day by day and gathered silver in abundance.

verses.rationale: Retains trades and the distinction between funding supervisors and workers.
verses.before: The king and Jehoiada gave it to those doing the work of the service of the house of the LORD. They hired stonecutters and craftsmen to repair the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to strengthen the house of the LORD.
verses.after: The king and Jehoiada gave the money to those overseeing the work on the LORD's house. They hired stonecutters and carpenters to restore it, as well as workers in iron and bronze to repair it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king and Jehoiada gave it to those doing the work of the service of the house of the LORD. They hired stonecutters and craftsmen to repair the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to strengthen the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Carries the healing/repair image naturally without inventing architectural specifications.
verses.before: Those doing the work labored, and the repair advanced in their hand. They restored the house of God according to its proper condition and strengthened it.
verses.after: The workers went about their tasks, and under their hands the repairs progressed. They restored God's house to its proper condition and made it strong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those doing the work labored, and the repair advanced in their hand. They restored the house of God according to its proper condition and strengthened it.

verses.rationale: Keeps surplus utensils here despite the Kings parallel, and repeats lifetime limit.
verses.before: When they had finished, they brought the rest of the silver before the king and Jehoiada, and they made from it vessels for the house of the LORD, vessels for service and for burnt offerings, dishes, and vessels of gold and silver. They offered burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually all the days of Jehoiada.
verses.after: When they finished, they brought the remaining money to the king and Jehoiada. It was used to make utensils for the LORD's house: utensils for service and burnt offerings, dishes, and gold and silver vessels. Burnt offerings were offered regularly in the LORD's house throughout Jehoiada's lifetime.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they had finished, they brought the rest of the silver before the king and Jehoiada, and they made from it vessels for the house of the LORD, vessels for service and for burnt offerings, dishes, and vessels of gold and silver. They offered burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually all the days of Jehoiada.

verses.rationale: Retains full-of-days image and exceptional age without correction.
verses.before: Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and he died. He was one hundred thirty years old when he died.
verses.after: Jehoiada grew old, full of days, and died. He was one hundred thirty years old when he died.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and he died. He was one hundred thirty years old when he died.

verses.rationale: Preserves royal burial's stated reason and prepares contrast with Joash.
verses.before: They buried him in the city of David with the kings because he had done good in Israel and toward God and his house.
verses.after: They buried him in the City of David with the kings, because he had done good in Israel, toward God and his house.
verses.tsw_comparator: They buried him in the city of David with the kings because he had done good in Israel and toward God and his house.

verses.rationale: Keeps the turning point and courtly gesture without guessing motives.
verses.before: After the death of Jehoiada, the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king. Then the king listened to them.
verses.after: After Jehoiada died, Judah's officials came and bowed before the king. Then the king listened to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the death of Jehoiada, the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king. Then the king listened to them.

verses.rationale: Retains corporate apostasy and wrath as the narrative's assessment.
verses.before: They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherah poles and idols. Wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem because of this guilt of theirs.
verses.after: They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherah poles and idols. Wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem because of this guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherah poles and idols. Wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem because of this guilt of theirs.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated refusal and purpose of prophetic sending.
verses.before: Yet he sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD. They testified against them, but they would not listen.
verses.after: He sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD. The prophets warned them, but they would not listen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet he sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD. They testified against them, but they would not listen.

verses.rationale: Preserves clothing image and the mirrored abandonment rather than smoothing its force.
verses.before: Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood above the people and said to them, “Thus says God: Why are you transgressing the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have abandoned the LORD, he has abandoned you.”
verses.after: Then God's Spirit clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood above the people and told them, “This is what God says: Why are you breaking the LORD's commands? You will not prosper. Because you have abandoned the LORD, he has abandoned you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood above the people and said to them, “Thus says God: Why are you transgressing the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have abandoned the LORD, he has abandoned you.”

verses.rationale: Names royal responsibility and sacred location of the killing.
verses.before: But they conspired against him and stoned him with stones at the king’s command in the court of the house of the LORD.
verses.after: They conspired against him and, at the king's command, stoned him in the court of the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they conspired against him and stoned him with stones at the king’s command in the court of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Clarifies fathers and sons while retaining remember, loyal love, and dying appeal.
verses.before: King Joash did not remember the steadfast love that Jehoiada his father had shown him, but killed his son. As he died, he said, “May the LORD see and seek justice.”
verses.after: King Joash did not remember the loyal love that Jehoiada, Zechariah's father, had shown him. Yet he killed Jehoiada's son. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “May the LORD see and call you to account!”
verses.tsw_comparator: King Joash did not remember the steadfast love that Jehoiada his father had shown him, but killed his son. As he died, he said, “May the LORD see and seek justice.”

verses.rationale: Retains seasonal phrasing and all officials without limiting destruction to defeat.
verses.before: And it happened at the turning of the year that the army of Aram came up against him. They came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the officials of the people from among the people and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.
verses.after: At the turn of the year, the Aramean army marched against Joash. They entered Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed all the people's officials, and sent all their plunder to the king of Damascus.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened at the turning of the year that the army of Aram came up against him. They came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the officials of the people from among the people and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.

verses.rationale: Preserves unequal numbers and narrative judgment without claiming Aramean moral superiority.
verses.before: Although the army of Aram came with a small number of men, the LORD gave into their hand a very great army because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors. So they executed judgment upon Joash.
verses.after: The Aramean army came with few men, yet the LORD handed over a very large army to them because Judah had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors. They executed judgment on Joash.
verses.tsw_comparator: Although the army of Aram came with a small number of men, the LORD gave into their hand a very great army because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors. So they executed judgment upon Joash.

verses.rationale: Retains plural sons in the Hebrew and burial exclusion; notes singular contextual difficulty.
verses.before: When they departed from him—for they left him with severe wounds—his servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest and killed him on his bed. He died, and they buried him in the city of David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
verses.after: When they withdrew, they left him gravely wounded. His servants conspired against him because of the blood of Jehoiada the priest's sons. They killed him on his bed, and he died. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the royal tombs.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they departed from him—for they left him with severe wounds—his servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest and killed him on his bed. He died, and they buried him in the city of David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.

verses.rationale: Preserves both maternal names, genders, and ethnic identifications without added inference.
verses.before: These are people who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
verses.after: Those who conspired against him were Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are those who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.

verses.rationale: Renders difficult increased-burden phrase as many pronouncements with alternative noted.
verses.before: As for his sons, the many pronouncements against him, and the foundation of the house of God, look, they are written in the commentary of the book of the kings. Amaziah his son became king in his place.
verses.after: The account of his sons, the many pronouncements against him, and the rebuilding of God's house is written in the exposition of the Book of the Kings. His son Amaziah succeeded him as king.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for his sons, the many pronouncements against him, and the foundation of the house of God, look, they are written in the commentary of the book of the kings. Amaziah his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Preserves both royal figures and the maternal name.
verses.before: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
verses.after: Amaziah was twenty-five when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps the inner qualification central to the ensuing reign.
verses.before: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not with a whole heart.
verses.after: He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, but not with an undivided heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not with a whole heart.

verses.rationale: Links consolidation to punishment without implying a new murder conspiracy.
verses.before: And it happened when the kingdom was firmly established for him that he put to death his servants who had struck his father the king.
verses.after: Once his hold on the kingdom was secure, he killed the servants who had struck down his father the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when the kingdom was firmly established for him that he put to death his servants who had struck his father the king.

verses.rationale: Retains specific sons and the quoted principle of individual liability.
verses.before: But he did not put their sons to death, according to what is written in the instruction, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, “Fathers will not be put to death for sons, and sons will not be put to death for fathers, but each person will die for his own sin.”
verses.after: But he did not put their sons to death, following what is written in the law, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not die for their children, and children must not die for their fathers. Each must die for his own sin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he did not put their sons to death, according to what is written in the instruction, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, “Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers, but each person shall die for his own sin.”

verses.rationale: Preserves age threshold, total, tribal scope, and two command levels.
verses.before: Amaziah gathered Judah and appointed them according to ancestral houses, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, throughout all Judah and Benjamin. He counted them from twenty years old and upward and found three hundred thousand choice men able to go out to war, handling spear and large shield.
verses.after: Amaziah assembled Judah and arranged all Judah and Benjamin by ancestral families under commanders of thousands and hundreds. He mustered the men twenty years old and upward and found three hundred thousand selected men fit for military service, able to handle spear and large shield.
verses.tsw_comparator: Amaziah gathered Judah and appointed them according to ancestral houses, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, throughout all Judah and Benjamin. He counted them from twenty years old and upward and found three hundred thousand choice men able to go out to war, handling spear and large shield.

verses.rationale: Keeps troop number, payment, and ancient weight unit distinct.
verses.before: He also hired from Israel one hundred thousand mighty warriors for one hundred talents of silver.
verses.after: He also hired one hundred thousand capable warriors from Israel for one hundred talents of silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: He also hired from Israel one hundred thousand mighty warriors for one hundred talents of silver.

verses.rationale: Retains the emphatic exclusion and the prophet's address without universalizing beyond the speech.
verses.before: But a man of God came to him, saying, “O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with all these children of Ephraim.
verses.after: But a man of God came to him and said, “King, do not let Israel's army go with you. The LORD is not with Israel—with any of the Ephraimites.
verses.tsw_comparator: But a man of God came to him, saying, “O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with all these children of Ephraim.

verses.rationale: Preserves abrupt imperatives and ensuing warning; notes disputed conditional force.
verses.before: But if you go, act, be strong for battle; God will make you stumble before the enemy, for God has power to help and to make stumble.”
verses.after: Go, then! Act! Be strong for battle! God will make you stumble before the enemy, for God has power both to help and to make people stumble.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you go, act, be strong for battle; God will make you stumble before the enemy, for God has power to help and to make stumble.”

verses.rationale: Maintains money question and direct answer, without turning it into a general prosperity promise.
verses.before: Amaziah said to the man of God, “And what about the one hundred talents that I gave to the troops of Israel?” The man of God said, “The LORD has much more than this to give you.”
verses.after: Amaziah asked the man of God, “What about the hundred talents I gave Israel's troops?” The man of God answered, “The LORD can give you much more than that.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Amaziah said to the man of God, “And what about the one hundred talents that I gave to the troops of Israel?” The man of God said, “The LORD has much more than this to give you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both anger descriptions and their target Judah.
verses.before: So Amaziah separated the troops who had come to him from Ephraim, that they should go to their place. Their anger burned greatly against Judah, and they returned to their place in fierce anger.
verses.after: So Amaziah dismissed the troops who had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home. They became furious with Judah and went home burning with anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Amaziah separated the troops who had come to him from Ephraim, that they should go to their place. Their anger burned greatly against Judah, and they returned to their place in fierce anger.

verses.rationale: Preserves named valley, Seir identity, and casualty figure.
verses.before: Amaziah strengthened himself and led his people and went to the Valley of Salt. He struck ten thousand of the children of Seir.
verses.after: Amaziah gathered his courage, led his people to the Valley of Salt, and struck down ten thousand men of Seir.
verses.tsw_comparator: Amaziah strengthened himself and led his people and went to the Valley of Salt. He struck ten thousand of the children of Seir.

verses.rationale: Retains atrocity against living prisoners and bodily outcome without euphemism.
verses.before: The children of Judah captured ten thousand alive and brought them to the top of the rock and threw them from the top of the rock, and all of them were broken to pieces.
verses.after: The men of Judah captured another ten thousand alive. They brought them to the top of a cliff and threw them down from it, and every one of them was torn apart.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Judah captured ten thousand alive and brought them to the top of the rock and threw them from the top of the rock, and all of them were broken to pieces.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult geographical span rather than silently substituting another city.
verses.before: But the men of the troop whom Amaziah had sent back from going with him to battle raided the cities of Judah from Samaria as far as Beth-Horon. They struck three thousand of them and took much plunder.
verses.after: Meanwhile, the troops Amaziah had sent back from going with him to battle raided Judah's cities, from Samaria to Beth-horon. They struck down three thousand people and took a great deal of plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the men of the troop whom Amaziah had sent back from going with him to battle raided the cities of Judah from Samaria as far as Beth-Horon. They struck three thousand of them and took much plunder.

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrative irony of adopting the defeated people's gods.
verses.before: After Amaziah came from striking the Edomites, he brought the gods of the children of Seir, set them up for himself as gods, bowed down before them, and burned incense to them.
verses.after: After Amaziah returned from striking down the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir and set them up as his own gods. He bowed before them and burned offerings to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: After Amaziah came from striking the Edomites, he brought the gods of the children of Seir, set them up for himself as gods, bowed down before them, and burned incense to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves seeking vocabulary and the prophet's pointed inability argument.
verses.before: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent a prophet to him who said to him, “Why have you sought the gods of the people who did not rescue their own people from your hand?”
verses.after: The LORD's anger burned against Amaziah. He sent him a prophet, who said, “Why have you sought the gods of a people whose gods could not rescue them from your hand?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent a prophet to him who said to him, “Why have you sought the gods of the people who did not rescue their own people from your hand?”

verses.rationale: Keeps threat and repeated counsel language in the exchange.
verses.before: And it happened as he spoke to him that the king said to him, “Have we appointed you as counselor to the king? Stop! Why should they strike you?” Then the prophet stopped, but said, “I know that God has determined to destroy you because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.”
verses.after: While the prophet was speaking, the king interrupted him: “Have we made you a royal adviser? Stop! Why should you be struck down?” The prophet stopped, but said, “I know God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my advice.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened as he spoke to him that the king said to him, “Have we appointed you as counselor to the king? Stop!
