verses.before: The children of Israel took captive from their brothers two hundred thousand—women, sons, and daughters—and also took much plunder from them and brought the spoil to Samaria.
verses.after: The Israelites took two hundred thousand captives from their own kin—women, sons, and daughters. They also seized a great deal of plunder and brought it to Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel took captive from their brothers two hundred thousand—women, sons, and daughters—and also took much plunder from them and brought the spoil to Samaria.

verses.rationale: Preserves prophetic indictment of victors despite divine handing over.
verses.before: But a prophet of the LORD was there whose name was Oded. He went out before the army coming to Samaria and said to them, “Look, because the LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah, he gave them into your hand, but you have killed them in a rage that has reached to the heavens.
verses.after: But a prophet of the LORD named Oded was there. He went out to meet the army returning to Samaria and said, “The LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah and handed them over to you. Yet you have slaughtered them in a rage that has reached heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: But a prophet of the LORD was there whose name was Oded. He went out before the army coming to Samaria and said to them, “Look, because the LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah, he gave them into your hand, but you have killed them in a rage that has reached to the heavens.

verses.rationale: Keeps gendered enslavement and the question exposing captors' guilt.
verses.before: And now you intend to subdue the children of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female servants for yourselves. But are there not with you also offenses against the LORD your God?
verses.after: And now you intend to force the people of Judah and Jerusalem into slavery as your men and women slaves. Do you not have guilt of your own before the LORD your God?
verses.tsw_comparator: And now you intend to subdue the children of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female servants for yourselves. But are there not with you also offenses against the LORD your God?

verses.rationale: Retains return imperative, kinship, and wrath directed at the victors.
verses.before: And now hear me and return the captives whom you captured from your brothers, for the burning anger of the LORD is upon you.”
verses.after: Listen to me now. Return the captives you have taken from your own kin, for the LORD's burning anger is against you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now hear me and return the captives whom you captured from your brothers, for the burning anger of the LORD is upon you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves all four named leaders and fathers.
verses.before: Then some men from the heads of the children of Ephraim—Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai—stood against those coming from the army.
verses.after: Some of the Ephraimite leaders confronted those returning from the army: Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then some men from the heads of the children of Ephraim—Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai—stood against those coming from the army.

verses.rationale: Keeps collective self-implication and repeated guilt language.
verses.before: They said to them, “You will not bring the captives here, for you intend to bring guilt upon us before the LORD, adding to our sins and our guilt, for our guilt is great, and burning anger is against Israel.”
verses.after: They told them, “You must not bring the captives here. What you propose will make us guilty before the LORD, adding to our sins and guilt. Our guilt is already great, and burning anger hangs over Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to them, “You shall not bring the captives here, for you intend to bring guilt upon us before the LORD, adding to our sins and our guilt, for our guilt is great, and burning anger is against Israel.”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes relinquishing people and goods without implying captives were abandoned helpless.
verses.before: So the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the officials and all the assembly.
verses.after: So the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the officials and the whole assembly.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the officials and all the assembly.

verses.rationale: Retains every concrete act of care, repeated clothing, and both destinations.
verses.before: The men who were designated by name arose and took the captives. From the spoil they clothed everyone who were naked among them, clothed them, gave them sandals, gave them food and drink, anointed them, carried all the weak on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, beside their brothers. Then they returned to Samaria.
verses.after: The men named above took charge of the captives. From the plunder they clothed everyone who was naked. They gave them clothes and sandals, food and drink, and rubbed them with oil. They put all who were weak on donkeys and brought them to their own kin at Jericho, the City of Palms. Then they returned to Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men who were designated by name arose and took the captives. From the spoil they clothed all who were naked among them, clothed them, gave them sandals, gave them food and drink, anointed them, carried all the weak on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, beside their brothers. Then they returned to Samaria.

verses.rationale: Retains Hebrew plural kings instead of silently substituting singular.
verses.before: At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.
verses.after: At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.

verses.rationale: Keeps renewed invasion and captivity in the background to the appeal.
verses.before: For the Edomites had come again and struck Judah and carried away captives.
verses.after: The Edomites had come again, attacked Judah, and taken captives.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Edomites had come again and struck Judah and carried away captives.

verses.rationale: Preserves all six cities and repeated dependent villages.
verses.before: The Philistines also raided the cities of the foothills and the Negev of Judah and captured Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages, and they lived there.
verses.after: The Philistines had raided the cities of Judah's foothills and Negev. They captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco and its villages, Timnah and its villages, and Gimzo and its villages, and settled there.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines also raided the cities of the foothills and the Negev of Judah and captured Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages, and they lived there.

verses.rationale: Retains source title Israel and distinguishes social disorder from covenant unfaithfulness.
verses.before: For the LORD humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had cast off restraint in Judah and acted very unfaithfully against the LORD.
verses.after: The LORD brought Judah low because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had let Judah run wild and had been utterly unfaithful to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had cast off restraint in Judah and acted very unfaithfully against the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves Chronicles' name form and failed military help.
verses.before: Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came against him and distressed him rather than strengthening him.
verses.after: Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came to him, but brought him distress instead of strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came against him and distressed him rather than strengthening him.

verses.rationale: Keeps three sources of tribute and the repeated failure of help.
verses.before: For Ahaz stripped the house of the LORD, the house of the king, and the officials and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him.
verses.after: Ahaz stripped resources from the LORD's house, the palace, and the officials and gave them to Assyria's king, but it did not help him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Ahaz stripped the house of the LORD, the house of the king, and the officials and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic same king and escalation under pressure.
verses.before: In the time of his distress he acted even more unfaithfully against the LORD—this King Ahaz.
verses.after: Even in his distress, this same King Ahaz became still more unfaithful to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the time of his distress he acted even more unfaithfully against the LORD—this King Ahaz.

verses.rationale: Keeps Ahaz's reasoning as his speech and narrator's contrary outcome.
verses.before: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had struck him and said, “Because the gods of the kings of Aram help them, I will sacrifice to them so that they may help me.” But they became his downfall and the downfall of all Israel.
verses.after: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus that had struck him, saying, “The gods of Aram's kings help them. I will sacrifice to those gods so they will help me.” But they brought about his downfall and that of all Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had struck him and said, “Because the gods of the kings of Aram help them, I will sacrifice to them so that they may help me.” But they became his downfall and the downfall of all Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves deliberate destruction and closed doors, setting up Hezekiah's reopening.
verses.before: Ahaz gathered the vessels of the house of God, cut the vessels of the house of God in pieces, shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and made for himself altars in every corner of Jerusalem.
verses.after: Ahaz gathered the utensils from God's house and cut them to pieces. He shut the doors of the LORD's house and made altars for himself on every corner of Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahaz gathered the vessels of the house of God, cut the vessels of the house of God in pieces, shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and made for himself altars in every corner of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps every-city scope and ancestral relationship in the assessment.
verses.before: In every city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods and provoked the LORD, the God of his ancestors, to anger.
verses.after: In every city of Judah he made high places for burning offerings to other gods. He provoked the LORD, the God of his ancestors, to anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: In every city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods and provoked the LORD, the God of his ancestors, to anger.

verses.rationale: Retains broad documentary summary without substituting later source titles.
verses.before: Now the rest of his acts and all his ways, first and last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.after: The rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of his acts and all his ways, first and last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps Israel's kings and burial exclusion, with successor clearly identified.
verses.before: Ahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, but they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. Hezekiah his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Ahaz rested with his ancestors. They buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, but did not bring him into the tombs of Israel's kings. His son Hezekiah succeeded him as king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, but they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. Hezekiah his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Preserves maternal name and genealogy alongside both reign figures.
verses.before: Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
verses.after: Hezekiah was twenty-five when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full Davidic comparison that contrasts with Ahaz.
verses.before: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD according to all that David his ancestor had done.
verses.after: He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, following all that his ancestor David had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD according to all that David his ancestor had done.

verses.rationale: Preserves both firsts and direct reversal of closed doors.
verses.before: In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
verses.after: In the first month of the first year of his reign, he opened the doors of the LORD's house and repaired them.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.

verses.rationale: Keeps separate groups and the specific meeting location.
verses.before: He brought in the priests and Levites and gathered them in the eastern square.
verses.after: He brought in the priests and Levites and assembled them in the eastern square.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought in the priests and Levites and gathered them in the eastern square.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated consecrate and removal as distinct requirements.
verses.before: He said to them, “Hear me, Levites! Now consecrate yourselves and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and bring out the uncleanness from the Holy Place.
verses.after: He told them, “Listen to me, Levites. Consecrate yourselves now, and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors. Remove the defilement from the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Hear me, Levites! Now consecrate yourselves and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and bring out the uncleanness from the Holy Place.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared confession and bodily face/back imagery.
verses.before: For our ancestors acted unfaithfully and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God. They abandoned him, turned their faces away from the dwelling place of the LORD, and turned their backs.
verses.after: Our ancestors were unfaithful and did what was evil in the LORD our God's eyes. They abandoned him, turned their faces away from the LORD's dwelling, and turned their backs on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For our ancestors acted unfaithfully and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God. They abandoned him, turned their faces away from the dwelling place of the LORD, and turned their backs.

verses.rationale: Preserves four suspended practices without reducing them to generic neglect.
verses.before: They also shut the doors of the porch, put out the lamps, and did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the Holy Place to the God of Israel.
verses.after: They even shut the porch doors and extinguished the lamps. They neither burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the sanctuary to Israel's God.
verses.tsw_comparator: They also shut the doors of the porch, put out the lamps, and did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the Holy Place to the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains three judgment terms and hissing's concrete image.
verses.before: So the wrath of the LORD was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them an object of terror, horror, and hissing, as you see with your eyes.
verses.after: So the LORD's wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem. He made them an object of horror, desolation, and hissing, as you can see with your own eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the wrath of the LORD was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them an object of terror, horror, and hissing, as you see with your eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps gender-specific family groups and the stated causal link.
verses.before: For look, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, daughters, and wives are in captivity because of this.
verses.after: Our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, daughters, and wives are in captivity because of this.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, daughters, and wives are in captivity because of this.

verses.rationale: Preserves heart, covenant, and corporate appeal for wrath to turn.
verses.before: Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that his burning anger may turn from us.
verses.after: Now I have set my heart on making a covenant with the LORD, Israel's God, so that his burning anger may turn away from us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that his burning anger may turn from us.

verses.rationale: Keeps paternal address and priestly standing/service vocabulary.
verses.before: My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him, to minister to him, to be his ministers, and to burn incense.”
verses.after: My sons, do not be negligent now. The LORD has chosen you to stand before him, to serve him as his ministers and to burn offerings.”
verses.tsw_comparator: My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him, to minister to him, to be his ministers, and to burn incense.”

verses.rationale: Preserves six names with fathers and three family divisions across the list.
verses.before: Then the Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the sons of the Kohathites; from the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; from the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
verses.after: These Levites arose: from the Kohathites, Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah; from Merari's descendants, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; from the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the sons of the Kohathites; from the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; from the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;

verses.rationale: Follows read Jeiel and maintains two family pairs.
verses.before: from the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; from the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
verses.after: from Elizaphan's descendants, Shimri and Jeiel; from Asaph's descendants, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; from the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;

verses.rationale: Follows read Jehiel and closes the remaining two pairs.
verses.before: from the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and from the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
verses.after: from Heman's descendants, Jehiel and Shimei; and from Jeduthun's descendants, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
verses.tsw_comparator: from the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and from the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.

verses.rationale: Makes brothers contextual fellow Levites while distinguishing royal and divine authority.
verses.before: They gathered their brothers, consecrated themselves, and went in according to the king’s command by the words of the LORD to cleanse the house of the LORD.
verses.after: They gathered their fellow Levites, consecrated themselves, and went in to cleanse the LORD's house, following the king's command in accordance with the LORD's words.
verses.tsw_comparator: They gathered their brothers, consecrated themselves, and went in according to the king’s command by the words of the LORD to cleanse the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves priests' inner access and Levites' outward disposal roles.
verses.before: The priests went into the inner part of the house of the LORD to cleanse it. They brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the temple of the LORD into the court of the house of the LORD, and the Levites took it out to the Wadi Kidron.
verses.after: The priests entered the inner part of the LORD's house to cleanse it. They brought everything unclean they found in the LORD's temple out into its court, and the Levites took it away to the Kidron Valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests went into the inner part of the house of the LORD to cleanse it. They brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the temple of the LORD into the court of the house of the LORD, and the Levites took it out to the Wadi Kidron.

verses.rationale: Retains first, eighth, and sixteenth days and two eight-day stages.
verses.before: They began to consecrate on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the porch of the LORD. They consecrated the house of the LORD for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
verses.after: They began the consecration on the first day of the first month and reached the LORD's porch on the eighth day. They consecrated the LORD's house for eight more days and finished on the sixteenth day of the first month.
verses.tsw_comparator: They began to consecrate on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the porch of the LORD. They consecrated the house of the LORD for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

verses.rationale: Keeps altar/table distinction and repeated complete equipment inventories.
verses.before: Then they went in to King Hezekiah and said, “We have cleansed all the house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and the table of the arrangement and all its vessels.
verses.after: Then they went in to King Hezekiah and said, “We have cleansed the entire house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the table for the arranged bread and all its utensils.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they went in to King Hezekiah and said, “We have cleansed all the house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and the table of the arrangement and all its vessels.

verses.rationale: Preserves restoration of rejected objects and present readiness.
verses.before: All the vessels that King Ahaz cast away during his reign when he acted unfaithfully, we have prepared and consecrated. And look, they are before the altar of the LORD.”
verses.after: We have prepared and consecrated all the utensils King Ahaz cast aside during his unfaithful reign. They are now before the LORD's altar.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the vessels that King Ahaz cast away during his reign when he acted unfaithfully, we have prepared and consecrated. And look, they are before the altar of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keeps early rising and ascent before sacrificial action.
verses.before: King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the officials of the city, and went up to the house of the LORD.
verses.after: King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the city's officials, and went up to the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the officials of the city, and went up to the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains four sets of seven and three beneficiaries without flattening ritual categories.
verses.before: They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. He commanded the sons of Aaron, the priests, to offer them upon the altar of the LORD.
verses.after: They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and Judah. He ordered the priests, Aaron's descendants, to offer them on the LORD's altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. He commanded the sons of Aaron, the priests, to offer them upon the altar of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated slaughter and blood handling rather than compressing ritual sequence.
verses.before: So they slaughtered the cattle, and the priests received the blood and threw it against the altar. They slaughtered the rams and threw the blood against the altar. They slaughtered the lambs and threw the blood against the altar.
verses.after: They slaughtered the cattle, and the priests received the blood and splashed it against the altar. They slaughtered the rams and splashed their blood against the altar. They slaughtered the lambs and splashed their blood against the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they slaughtered the cattle, and the priests received the blood and threw it against the altar. They slaughtered the rams and threw the blood against the altar. They slaughtered the lambs and threw the blood against the altar.

verses.rationale: Makes king and assembly the hand-laying participants.
verses.before: Then they brought the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands upon them.
verses.after: They brought the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, who laid their hands on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they brought the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands upon them.

verses.rationale: Preserves atonement and emphatically repeated all Israel.
verses.before: The priests slaughtered them and made purification with their blood upon the altar to make atonement for all Israel, for the king had said that the burnt offering and sin offering were for all Israel.
verses.after: The priests slaughtered them and applied their blood to the altar as a sin offering, to make atonement for all Israel. The king had ordered both the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests slaughtered them and made purification with their blood upon the altar to make atonement for all Israel, for the king had said that the burnt offering and sin offering were for all Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps three authorities and instruments, with ultimate source explicit.
verses.before: He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres according to the command of David, Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet, for the command was by the hand of the LORD through his prophets.
verses.after: He stationed the Levites in the LORD's house with cymbals, harps, and lyres, following the command of David, Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet. The command came from the LORD through his prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres according to the command of David, Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet, for the command was by the hand of the LORD through his prophets.

verses.rationale: Retains distinct musical assignments in a compact balanced sentence.
verses.before: The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.
verses.after: The Levites stood with David's instruments, and the priests with the trumpets.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

verses.rationale: Keeps coordinated onset of sacrifice, song, trumpets, and instruments.
verses.before: Hezekiah commanded that the burnt offering be offered upon the altar. At the time the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD began, and the trumpets, together with the instruments of David king of Israel.
verses.after: Hezekiah ordered the burnt offering to be offered on the altar. As it began, the song to the LORD began too, with trumpets accompanied by the instruments of David king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hezekiah commanded that the burnt offering be offered upon the altar. At the time the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD began, and the trumpets, together with the instruments of David king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves simultaneous threefold activity and its duration.
verses.before: All the assembly bowed down while the song was sung and the trumpets sounded. All this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
verses.after: The whole assembly bowed in worship, the singers sang, and the trumpets sounded. All this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the assembly bowed down while the song was sung and the trumpets sounded. All this continued until the burnt offering was finished.

verses.rationale: Retains kneeling and worship after the completed offering.
verses.before: When they finished offering, the king and everyone who were present with him bowed and worshiped.
verses.after: When the offering was finished, the king and everyone with him knelt and bowed in worship.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they finished offering, the king and all who were present with him bowed and worshiped.

verses.rationale: Keeps attributed words, joy, and bodily response.
verses.before: King Hezekiah and the officials commanded the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and Asaph the seer. They praised with gladness and bowed down and worshiped.
verses.after: King Hezekiah and the officials told the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and Asaph the seer. They praised him joyfully, then bowed their heads and worshiped.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Hezekiah and the officials commanded the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and Asaph the seer. They praised with gladness and bowed down and worshiped.

verses.rationale: Renders filled-hands idiom with vocabulary explanation; preserves willing-heart distinction.
verses.before: Then Hezekiah answered and said, “Now you have filled your hands for the LORD. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD.” The assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and every willing heart brought burnt offerings.
verses.after: Then Hezekiah said, “Now you have consecrated yourselves to the LORD. Come forward and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the LORD's house.” The assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and everyone with a willing heart brought burnt offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Hezekiah answered and said, “Now you have filled your hands for the LORD. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD.” The assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and every willing heart brought burnt offerings.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact three-category burnt-offering count.
