verses.rationale: Keeps outlying residents, designated distributors, and male priestly eligibility.
verses.before: And for the sons of Aaron, the priests, in the fields of the pasturelands of their cities, in every city, men who were designated by name gave portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites.
verses.after: For Aaron's descendants, the priests living in the pasturelands around their cities, men were designated by name in each city to give portions to every male among the priests and everyone registered among the Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: And for the sons of Aaron, the priests, in the fields of the pasturelands of their cities, in every city, men who were designated by name gave portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites.

verses.rationale: Retains the threefold positive judgment as a whole-reign summary here.
verses.before: Thus Hezekiah did throughout all Judah. He did what was good and right and faithful before the LORD his God.
verses.after: This is what Hezekiah did throughout Judah. He did what was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus Hezekiah did throughout all Judah. He did what was good and right and faithful before the LORD his God.

verses.rationale: Keeps wholehearted seeking tied to actual work and success.
verses.before: In every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the instruction and the commandment, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart and prospered.
verses.after: In everything he undertook for the service of God's house and for the law and commands, he sought his God with all his heart. He did the work and prospered.
verses.tsw_comparator: In every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the instruction and the commandment, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart and prospered.

verses.rationale: Preserves invasion after faithfulness rather than implying prior wrongdoing caused it.
verses.before: After these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah. He camped against the fortified cities and intended to break into them for himself.
verses.after: After these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He encamped against the fortified cities, intending to break into them and take them for himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: After these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah. He camped against the fortified cities and intended to break into them for himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps the king's perception of Assyrian intent.
verses.before: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and that his face was set for war against Jerusalem,
verses.after: Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and was intent on making war against Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and that his face was set for war against Jerusalem,

verses.rationale: Retains consultation and collaborative water defense.
verses.before: he took counsel with his officials and mighty men to stop the waters of the springs that were outside the city, and they helped him.
verses.after: He consulted his officials and warriors about stopping up the springs outside the city, and they helped him.
verses.tsw_comparator: he took counsel with his officials and mighty men to stop the waters of the springs that were outside the city, and they helped him.

verses.rationale: Preserves all water sources and plural kings in the rationale.
verses.before: Many people gathered, and they stopped all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land, saying, “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?”
verses.after: A large crowd gathered and stopped up all the springs and the stream flowing through the land. They said, “Why should Assyria's kings come and find abundant water?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Many people gathered, and they stopped all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land, saying, “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?”

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult tower construction phrasing and all defensive works.
verses.before: He strengthened himself, rebuilt all the wall that was broken, raised towers upon it, and built another wall outside. He strengthened the Millo of the city of David and made weapons and shields in abundance.
verses.after: He acted resolutely. He rebuilt the whole broken wall and raised it to the towers, built another wall outside it, strengthened the Millo in the City of David, and made many weapons and shields.
verses.tsw_comparator: He strengthened himself, rebuilt all the wall that was broken, raised towers upon it, and built another wall outside. He strengthened the Millo of the city of David and made weapons and shields in abundance.

verses.rationale: Keeps heart-address image and the assembly's location before direct speech.
verses.before: He appointed commanders of war over the people, gathered them to himself in the square at the city gate, and spoke to their heart, saying,
verses.after: He appointed military commanders over the people and gathered them to him in the square at the city gate. He spoke to their hearts:
verses.tsw_comparator: He appointed commanders of war over the people, gathered them to himself in the square at the city gate, and spoke to their heart, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves open more-with-us comparison rather than supplying unseen troops.
verses.before: “Be strong and courageous. Do not fear or be dismayed before the king of Assyria and before all the multitude that is with him, for there are more with us than with him.
verses.after: “Be strong and courageous. Do not fear or lose heart before Assyria's king and the whole multitude with him. There is more with us than with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Be strong and courageous. Do not fear or be dismayed before the king of Assyria and before all the multitude that is with him, for there are more with us than with him.

verses.rationale: Retains arm-of-flesh and leaning images with brief vocabulary explanation.
verses.before: With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles.” And the people leaned upon the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
verses.after: With him is an arm of flesh; with us is the LORD our God, to help us and fight our battles.” The people leaned on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles.” And the people leaned upon the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps siege setting and both intended audiences.
verses.before: After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem—while he and all his royal force were against Lachish—to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying,
verses.after: After this, while Sennacherib king of Assyria was at Lachish with all his forces, he sent his servants to Jerusalem with a message for Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah in Jerusalem:
verses.tsw_comparator: After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem—while he and all his royal force were against Lachish—to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves challenge to trust as the organizing question.
verses.before: “Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: On what are you trusting, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
verses.after: “This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: What are you trusting in, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: On what are you trusting, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?

verses.rationale: Keeps threatened bodily deprivation and quoted promise as enemy rhetoric.
verses.before: Is not Hezekiah misleading you, to give you over to die by famine and thirst, saying, ‘The LORD our God will rescue us from the hand of the king of Assyria’?
verses.after: Isn't Hezekiah misleading you, handing you over to die of hunger and thirst when he says, ‘The LORD our God will rescue us from Assyria's king’?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not Hezekiah misleading you, to give you over to die by famine and thirst, saying, ‘The LORD our God will rescue us from the hand of the king of Assyria’?

verses.rationale: Retains Assyrian interpretation of centralization without endorsing it narratively.
verses.before: Is not this Hezekiah the one who removed his high places and his altars and said to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘Before one altar you will bow down, and upon it you will burn incense’?
verses.after: Wasn't it Hezekiah himself who removed his high places and altars and told Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must bow before one altar and burn offerings on it’?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not this Hezekiah the one who removed his high places and his altars and said to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘Before one altar you shall bow down, and upon it you shall burn incense’?

verses.rationale: Preserves boast, ancestors, and question about land rescue.
verses.before: Do you not know what I and my ancestors have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands at all able to rescue their land from my hand?
verses.after: Do you not know what I and my ancestors have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of those nations able to rescue their lands from my hand?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you not know what I and my ancestors have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands at all able to rescue their land from my hand?

verses.rationale: Keeps destruction language and repeated hand/rescue challenge.
verses.before: Who was there among all the gods of those nations that my ancestors devoted to destruction who could rescue his people from my hand, that your God should be able to rescue you from my hand?
verses.after: Which god among all those nations my ancestors devoted to destruction could rescue his people from my hand? How then could your God rescue you from my hand?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who was there among all the gods of those nations that my ancestors devoted to destruction who was able to rescue his people from my hand, that your God should be able to rescue you from my hand?

verses.rationale: Retains escalating denial and repeated rescue rather than shortening the taunt.
verses.before: And now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and do not trust him, for no god of any nation or kingdom could rescue his people from my hand or from the hand of my ancestors. How much less will your God rescue you from my hand!”
verses.after: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this. Do not believe him. No god of any nation or kingdom has been able to rescue his people from my hand or my ancestors' hands. How much less will your God rescue you from my hand!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and do not trust him, for no god of any nation or kingdom was able to rescue his people from my hand or from the hand of my ancestors. How much less will your God rescue you from my hand!”

verses.rationale: Keeps God and Hezekiah as distinct targets, with servant relationship explicit.
verses.before: His servants spoke still more against the LORD God and against Hezekiah his servant.
verses.after: His servants said still more against the LORD God and against his servant Hezekiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: His servants spoke still more against the LORD God and against Hezekiah his servant.

verses.rationale: Preserves written insult and repeated comparison in full.
verses.before: He also wrote letters to taunt the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the lands did not rescue their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not rescue his people from my hand.”
verses.after: Sennacherib also wrote letters insulting the LORD, Israel's God: “Just as the gods of the nations could not rescue their people from my hand, Hezekiah's God will not rescue his people from my hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He also wrote letters to taunt the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the lands did not rescue their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not rescue his people from my hand.”

verses.rationale: Keeps local language and psychological purpose without modernizing to an unrelated language.
verses.before: They called with a loud voice in Judean to the people of Jerusalem who were upon the wall, to frighten and terrify them, so that they might capture the city.
verses.after: They shouted loudly in the language of Judah to Jerusalem's people on the wall, trying to frighten and terrify them so they could capture the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: They called with a loud voice in Judean to the people of Jerusalem who were upon the wall, to frighten and terrify them, so that they might capture the city.

verses.rationale: Preserves narrator's distinction and handmade-gods image.
verses.before: They spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
verses.after: They spoke of Jerusalem's God as though he were like the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: They spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.

verses.rationale: Keeps two named petitioners and heavenward cry.
verses.before: Then King Hezekiah and Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz prayed concerning this and cried to the heavens.
verses.after: Because of this, King Hezekiah and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet prayed and cried out to heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Hezekiah and Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz prayed concerning this and cried to the heavens.

verses.rationale: Keeps three victim groups and offspring, without importing Kings' numbers or sons' names.
verses.before: The LORD sent a messenger who cut off every mighty warrior, commander, and officer in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land. When he entered the house of his god, some who came from his own body struck him down there with the sword.
verses.after: The LORD sent an angel who wiped out every capable warrior, leader, and commander in Assyria's camp. Sennacherib returned to his land with shame on his face. When he entered his god's house, some of his own offspring struck him down there with the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD sent a messenger who cut off every mighty warrior, commander, and officer in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land. When he entered the house of his god, some who came from his own body struck him down there with the sword.

verses.rationale: Retains guided rather than replacing the Hebrew with gave-rest alternative.
verses.before: Thus the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all others and gave them rest on every side.
verses.after: So the LORD saved Hezekiah and Jerusalem's inhabitants from Sennacherib king of Assyria and from everyone else. He guided them on every side.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all others and gave them rest on every side.

verses.rationale: Keeps distinct recipients and resulting international esteem.
verses.before: Many brought gifts to the LORD at Jerusalem and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah, and he was lifted up in the eyes of all the nations after this.
verses.after: Many brought offerings to the LORD in Jerusalem and precious gifts to Hezekiah king of Judah. From then on he was held high in the eyes of all the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many brought gifts to the LORD at Jerusalem and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah, and he was lifted up in the eyes of all the nations after this.

verses.rationale: Preserves compressed report without importing added years or the sign's form.
verses.before: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. He prayed to the LORD, and he spoke to him and gave him a sign.
verses.after: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill and prayed to the LORD. The LORD answered him and gave him a sign.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. He prayed to the LORD, and he spoke to him and gave him a sign.

verses.rationale: Keeps ingratitude, pride, and corporate consequences without specifying unreported actions.
verses.before: Yet Hezekiah did not return according to the benefit done to him, for his heart became high. Therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.after: But Hezekiah did not respond in keeping with the benefit he had received, because his heart grew proud. Wrath came upon him, Judah, and Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Hezekiah did not return according to the benefit done to him, for his heart became high. Therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves shared humbling and temporal limit of delayed wrath.
verses.before: Then Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
verses.after: Then Hezekiah humbled himself over his proud heart, and Jerusalem's inhabitants did too. The LORD's wrath did not come upon them during Hezekiah's lifetime.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.

verses.rationale: Retains full wealth inventory and sentence continuing into storage arrangements.
verses.before: Hezekiah had very great riches and honor. He made for himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of desirable vessels;
verses.after: Hezekiah had very great wealth and honor. He made treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and every kind of valuable article,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hezekiah had very great riches and honor. He made for himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of desirable vessels;

verses.rationale: Renders difficult final livestock phrase contextually while retaining all agricultural categories.
verses.before: storehouses also for the produce of grain, new wine, and oil, stalls for every kind of livestock, and flocks in folds.
verses.after: storehouses for the harvest of grain, new wine, and oil, stalls for every kind of livestock, and folds for flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: storehouses also for the produce of grain, new wine, and oil, stalls for every kind of livestock, and flocks in folds.

verses.rationale: Retains cities as pinned rather than substituting flocks or enclosures.
verses.before: He made cities for himself and acquired flocks and herds in abundance, for God had given him very many possessions.
verses.after: He built cities for himself and acquired abundant flocks and herds, for God gave him very great possessions.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made cities for himself and acquired flocks and herds in abundance, for God had given him very many possessions.

verses.rationale: Keeps direction and outlet without claiming a specific archaeological identification.
verses.before: This Hezekiah stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them downward to the west side of the city of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his work.
verses.after: It was Hezekiah who stopped up the upper outlet of Gihon's waters and directed them down westward to the City of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his work.
verses.tsw_comparator: This Hezekiah stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them downward to the west side of the city of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his work.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine leaving and knowing-purpose without theological mitigation.
verses.before: And so with the envoys of the officials of Babylon, who had been sent to him to inquire concerning the sign that had happened in the land, God left him to himself to test him, to know all that was in his heart.
verses.after: But when the envoys of Babylon's rulers came to him to inquire about the sign that had happened in the land, God left him to test him and to know everything in his heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: And so with the envoys of the officials of Babylon, who had been sent to him to inquire concerning the sign that had happened in the land, God left him to himself to test him, to know all that was in his heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps loyal-love deeds and nested documentary attribution.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his steadfast deeds, look, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.after: The rest of Hezekiah's acts and his deeds of loyal love are written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his steadfast deeds, look, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains ascent's spatial ambiguity and public honor rather than ordinary tomb formula.
verses.before: Hezekiah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him on the ascent to the tombs of the sons of David. All Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem honored him at his death. Manasseh his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Hezekiah rested with his ancestors. They buried him on the ascent to the tombs of David's descendants, and all Judah and Jerusalem's inhabitants honored him at his death. His son Manasseh succeeded him as king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hezekiah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him on the ascent to the tombs of the sons of David. All Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem honored him at his death. Manasseh his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Preserves youthful accession and fifty-five-year reign.
verses.before: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
verses.after: Manasseh was twelve when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for fifty-five years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator's comparison and displacement background.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD according to the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the children of Israel.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD according to the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains reversal, multiple cult objects, and heavenly-host image.
verses.before: He rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had torn down, raised altars for the Baals, made Asherah poles, and bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.
verses.after: He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had demolished, set up altars for the Baals, made Asherah poles, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had torn down, raised altars for the Baals, made Asherah poles, and bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contradiction between altars and enduring name promise.
verses.before: He built altars in the house of the LORD, concerning which the LORD had said, “In Jerusalem my name will be forever.”
verses.after: He built altars in the LORD's house, where the LORD had said, “My name will be in Jerusalem forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He built altars in the house of the LORD, concerning which the LORD had said, “In Jerusalem my name shall be forever.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both courts and the repeated heavenly host.
verses.before: He built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of the LORD.
verses.after: He built altars for all the host of heaven in both courts of the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains passage-through-fire wording with sacrificial meaning explained; keeps distinct forbidden practices.
verses.before: He made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, practiced soothsaying, divination, and sorcery, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He multiplied doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.
verses.after: He made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom. He practiced divination, sought omens, used sorcery, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He did much evil in the LORD's eyes, provoking him to anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, practiced soothsaying, divination, and sorcery, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He multiplied doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.

verses.rationale: Keeps both recipients and repeated house/name/forever rather than summarizing.
verses.before: He set the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.
verses.after: He put the carved idol he had made in God's house, about which God had told David and his son Solomon: “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all Israel's tribes, I will place my name forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: He set the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves feet/soil imagery and explicit condition on remaining in the land.
verses.before: I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the ground that I appointed for your ancestors, if only they are careful to do all that I commanded them, all the instruction, statutes, and judgments by the hand of Moses.”
verses.after: I will no longer remove Israel's feet from the soil I appointed for your ancestors, if only they carefully do everything I commanded them—all the law, statutes, and judgments given through Moses.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the ground that I appointed for your ancestors, if only they are careful to do all that I commanded them, all the instruction, statutes, and judgments by the hand of Moses.”

verses.rationale: Keeps intensified comparative judgment without softening national responsibility.
verses.before: Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the children of Israel.
verses.after: Manasseh led Judah and Jerusalem's inhabitants astray, so that they did worse evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed before Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains both addressees and refusal without inventing the speech's content.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they did not listen.
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they paid no attention.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they did not listen.

verses.rationale: Keeps hooks, bronze restraints, and Babylon despite Assyrian captors.
verses.before: So the LORD brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria. They captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze chains, and brought him to Babylon.
verses.after: So the LORD brought against them the army commanders of Assyria's king. They captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him in bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the LORD brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria. They captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze chains, and brought him to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Retains distress, favor-seeking, and deep humbling without embellishing repentance.
verses.before: When he was in distress, he sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his ancestors.
verses.after: In his distress he sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself deeply before the God of his ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he was in distress, he sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his ancestors.

verses.rationale: Makes divine hearer clear and preserves restoration leading to recognition.
verses.before: He prayed to him, and God was entreated by him and heard his plea and brought him back to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD—he is God.
verses.after: He prayed to him, and God received his plea, heard his appeal, and brought him back to Jerusalem to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.
verses.tsw_comparator: He prayed to him, and God was entreated by him and heard his plea and brought him back to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD—he is God.

verses.rationale: Keeps height, route, named landmarks, and garrison coverage.
verses.before: After this he built an outer wall for the city of David west of Gihon in the valley, as far as the entrance of the Fish Gate, encircling Ophel, and he made it very high. He also put commanders of the army in all the fortified cities of Judah.
verses.after: Afterward he built a very high outer wall for the City of David, west of Gihon in the valley, extending to the entrance of the Fish Gate and around the Ophel. He stationed army commanders in all Judah's fortified cities.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this he built an outer wall for the city of David west of Gihon in the valley, as far as the entrance of the Fish Gate, encircling Ophel, and he made it very high. He also put commanders of the army in all the fortified cities of Judah.

verses.rationale: Preserves two locations and physical disposal without conflating all objects into one idol.
verses.before: He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and he threw them outside the city.
verses.after: He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the LORD's house, along with all the altars he had built on the mountain of the LORD's house and in Jerusalem, and threw them outside the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and he threw them outside the city.

verses.rationale: Follows read rebuilt instead of written established; retains both offering types.
verses.before: He restored the altar of the LORD and sacrificed upon it offerings of well-being and thanksgiving, and commanded Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.after: He rebuilt the LORD's altar and sacrificed well-being offerings and thank offerings on it. He told Judah to serve the LORD, Israel's God.
verses.tsw_comparator: He restored the altar of the LORD and sacrificed upon it offerings of well-being and thanksgiving, and commanded Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps lingering high places and changed recipient together.
verses.before: Even so the people still sacrificed on the high places, but only to the LORD their God.
verses.after: The people still sacrificed at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless the people still sacrificed on the high places, but only to the LORD their God.

verses.rationale: Retains prayer and prophetic words as separate recorded material.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, look, they are in the acts of the kings of Israel.
verses.after: The rest of Manasseh's acts, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, Israel's God, are in the records of Israel's kings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, look, they are in the acts of the kings of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains Hozai as pointed name with alternative seers in note, not silent substitution.
verses.before: His prayer and how God was entreated by him, all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up the Asherah poles and carved images before he humbled himself, look, they are written in the words of Hozai.
verses.after: His prayer and how it was answered, all his sin and unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and carved images before he humbled himself are written in the records of Hozai.
verses.tsw_comparator: His prayer and how God was entreated by him, all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up the Asherah poles and carved images before he humbled himself, look, they are written in the words of Hozai.

verses.rationale: Keeps house burial rather than adding a named garden from Kings.
verses.before: Manasseh lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in his house. Amon his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Manasseh rested with his ancestors and was buried at his house. His son Amon succeeded him as king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Manasseh lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in his house. Amon his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Preserves both accession and short reign figures.
verses.before: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
verses.after: Amon was twenty-two when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for two years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated paternal connection and actual objects of worship.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD as Manasseh his father had done. Amon sacrificed to all the carved images that Manasseh his father had made and served them.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, as his father Manasseh had done. Amon sacrificed to all the carved images his father had made and served them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD as Manasseh his father had done. Amon sacrificed to all the carved images that Manasseh his father had made and served them.

verses.rationale: Preserves decisive contrast and emphatic personal responsibility.
verses.before: He did not humble himself before the LORD as Manasseh his father had humbled himself, but this Amon multiplied guilt.
verses.after: But he did not humble himself before the LORD as his father Manasseh had. This Amon multiplied his guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did not humble himself before the LORD as Manasseh his father had humbled himself, but this Amon multiplied guilt.

verses.rationale: Keeps perpetrators and domestic location without importing motives.
verses.before: His servants conspired against him and put him to death in his house.
verses.after: His servants conspired against him and killed him in his own house.
verses.tsw_comparator: His servants conspired against him and put him to death in his house.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated public agency and lethal retaliation before succession.
verses.before: But the people of the land struck everyone who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
verses.after: The people of the land struck down everyone who had conspired against King Amon. Then the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the people of the land struck all who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.

verses.rationale: Preserves age eight and thirty-one-year reign.
verses.before: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
verses.after: Josiah was eight when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-one years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps path and directional image rather than flattening to obedience.
verses.before: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the ways of David his ancestor. He did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.after: He did what was right in the LORD's eyes and followed the ways of his ancestor David, turning neither right nor left.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the ways of David his ancestor. He did not turn aside to the right or to the left.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes eighth-year seeking and twelfth-year cleansing with all object categories.
verses.before: In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his ancestor. In the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, Asherah poles, carved images, and cast images.
verses.after: In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David. In the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, Asherah poles, carved images, and cast images.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his ancestor. In the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, Asherah poles, carved images, and cast images.

verses.rationale: Preserves sequence of destruction and deliberate grave defilement.
verses.before: They tore down the altars of the Baals before him, and he cut down the incense altars that were above them. He shattered the Asherah poles, carved images, and cast images, ground them to powder, and scattered it upon the graves of people who had sacrificed to them.
verses.after: They demolished the Baals' altars in his presence. He cut down the incense altars above them, smashed the Asherah poles and the carved and cast images, ground them to powder, and scattered it over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They tore down the altars of the Baals before him, and he cut down the incense altars that were above them. He shattered the Asherah poles, carved images, and cast images, ground them to powder, and scattered it upon the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps burning human bones explicit and the narrator's cleansing framework.
verses.before: He burned the bones of the priests upon their altars and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.after: He burned the priests' bones on their altars. In this way he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: He burned the bones of the priests upon their altars and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Follows read ruins while preserving four tribal locations and continuing syntax.
verses.before: In the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, among their ruins all around,
verses.after: In the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, and in their surrounding ruins,
verses.tsw_comparator: In the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, among their ruins all around,

verses.rationale: Retains northern extent and return after the full destruction inventory.
verses.before: he tore down the altars, beat the Asherah poles and carved images into powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.after: he demolished the altars, crushed the Asherah poles and carved images to powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout Israel's land. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: he tore down the altars, beat the Asherah poles and carved images into powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps eighteenth-year setting and all three named officials with roles.
verses.before: In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had cleansed the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah ruler of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD his God.
verses.after: In the eighteenth year of his reign, as he cleansed the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the city governor, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had cleansed the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah ruler of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD his God.

verses.rationale: Follows read returned, recording written Jerusalem-inhabitants alternative in note.
verses.before: They came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave the silver that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites who guarded the threshold had gathered from Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.after: They came to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the money brought into God's house. The Levite gatekeepers had collected it from Manasseh and Ephraim, from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave the silver that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites who guarded the threshold had gathered from Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Makes two-stage payment flow clear without conflating supervisors and workers.
verses.before: They gave it into the hand of those doing the work who were appointed over the house of the LORD, and those doing the work in the house of the LORD gave it to repair and strengthen the house.
verses.after: They gave it to the supervisors of the work in the LORD's house, who passed it to the workers repairing and restoring the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: They gave it into the hand of those doing the work who were appointed over the house of the LORD, and those doing the work in the house of the LORD gave it to repair and strengthen the house.

verses.rationale: Keeps building materials and royal responsibility without inventing particular damage events.
verses.before: They gave it to the craftsmen and builders to buy quarried stone and timber for beams and to floor the houses that the kings of Judah had allowed to decay.
verses.after: They gave it to carpenters and builders to buy quarried stone and timber for joints and beams for the buildings Judah's kings had ruined.
verses.tsw_comparator: They gave it to the craftsmen and builders to buy quarried stone and timber for beams and to floor the houses that the kings of Judah had allowed to decay.

verses.rationale: Preserves four supervisors and lineages while allowing musicians' role to continue into next verse.
verses.before: The men were doing the work faithfully. Over them were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites from the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the sons of the Kohathites, to oversee. Other Levites, all skilled with musical instruments,
verses.after: The men worked faithfully. Their supervisors were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites descended from Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, descended from Kohath. The Levites skilled with musical instruments
verses.tsw_comparator: The men were doing the work faithfully. Over them were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites from the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the sons of the Kohathites, to oversee. Other Levites, all skilled with musical instruments,

verses.rationale: Keeps manual-work oversight and three other administrative roles.
verses.before: were over the burden-bearers and directed everyone who did work in every kind of service. Some of the Levites were scribes, officers, and gatekeepers.
verses.after: were also over the burden-bearers and supervised all the workers in every kind of service. Some Levites served as scribes, officers, and gatekeepers.
verses.tsw_comparator: were over the burden-bearers and directed all who did work in every kind of service. Some of the Levites were scribes, officers, and gatekeepers.

verses.rationale: Retains discovery during financial work and through-Moses attribution.
verses.before: When they brought out the silver that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the instruction of the LORD given by the hand of Moses.
verses.after: While they were bringing out the money contributed to the LORD's house, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the LORD's law given through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they brought out the silver that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the instruction of the LORD given by the hand of Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves report and physical transfer without prematurely describing its contents.
verses.before: Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the book of the instruction in the house of the LORD.” And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
verses.after: Hilkiah told Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the book of the law in the LORD's house.” Then he gave the book to Shaphan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the book of the instruction in the house of the LORD.” And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.

verses.rationale: Keeps book delivery distinct from preliminary work report.
verses.before: Shaphan brought the book to the king and also returned a word to the king, saying, “All that was given into the hand of your servants, they are doing.
verses.after: Shaphan brought the book to the king and also reported, “Your servants are doing everything entrusted to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shaphan brought the book to the king and also returned a word to the king, saying, “All that was given into the hand of your servants, they are doing.

verses.rationale: Retains poured-out verb with note on monetary handling rather than claiming minting.
verses.before: They have poured out the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and have given it into the hand of those appointed and into the hand of those doing the work.”
verses.after: They have poured out the money found in the LORD's house and handed it to the supervisors and workers.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They have poured out the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and have given it into the hand of those appointed and into the hand of those doing the work.”

verses.rationale: Preserves restrained a-book introduction and public reading act.
verses.before: Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.” And Shaphan read from it before the king.
verses.after: Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.” And Shaphan read from it before the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.” And Shaphan read from it before the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing as immediate trigger of bodily grief.
verses.before: And it happened when the king heard the words of the instruction that he tore his clothes.
verses.after: When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when the king heard the words of the instruction that he tore his clothes.

verses.rationale: Preserves all five delegates and Chronicles' Abdon name.
verses.before: The king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah servant of the king, saying,
verses.after: The king gave orders to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king's servant:
verses.tsw_comparator: The king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah servant of the king, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps remnant scope, inquiry, and poured-out wrath without moving all responsibility to the past.
verses.before: “Go, inquire of the LORD for me and for people who remain in Israel and Judah concerning the words of the book that has been found, for great is the wrath of the LORD that is poured out upon us because our ancestors did not keep the word of the LORD, to do according to all that is written in this book.”
verses.after: “Go and inquire of the LORD for me and for those left in Israel and Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found. Great is the LORD's wrath poured out on us, because our ancestors have not kept the LORD's word by doing everything written in this book.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go, inquire of the LORD for me and for those who remain in Israel and Judah concerning the words of the book that has been found, for great is the wrath of the LORD that is poured out upon us because our ancestors did not keep the word of the LORD, to do according to all that is written in this book.”

verses.rationale: Preserves female prophetic authority and husband's lineage; uses conventional Tokhath for read Takhat.
verses.before: So Hilkiah and those whom the king had appointed went to Huldah the prophet, wife of Shallum son of Tokhath son of Hasrah, keeper of the garments. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter, and they spoke to her concerning this.
verses.after: Hilkiah and those the king had sent went to Huldah the prophet, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem's Second Quarter. They spoke to her about this.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Hilkiah and those whom the king had appointed went to Huldah the prophet, wife of Shallum son of Tokhath son of Hasrah, keeper of the garments. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter, and they spoke to her concerning this.

verses.rationale: Keeps Huldah speaking with divine authority and the king called the man.
verses.before: She said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
verses.after: She told them, “This is what the LORD, Israel's God, says: Tell the man who sent you to me,
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,

verses.rationale: Preserves all curses and both land and inhabitants as recipients.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am bringing disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the curses written in the book that they read before the king of Judah,
verses.after: ‘This is what the LORD says: I am bringing disaster on this place and its inhabitants—all the curses written in the book read before Judah's king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am bringing disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the curses written in the book that they read before the king of Judah,

verses.rationale: Retains pouring and unquenchable imagery without harmonizing mixed metaphors.
verses.before: because they abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, provoking me to anger with all the work of their hands. My wrath will be poured out upon this place and will not be extinguished.
verses.after: They have abandoned me and burned offerings to other gods, provoking me with everything their hands have made. My wrath will pour out on this place and will not be quenched.’
verses.tsw_comparator: because they abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, provoking me to anger with all the work of their hands. My wrath will be poured out upon this place and will not be extinguished.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes second message to the responsive king from national judgment.
verses.before: But to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus you will say to him: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the words that you heard:
verses.after: But say this to Judah's king, who sent you to inquire of the LORD: ‘This is what the LORD, Israel's God, says about the words you heard:
verses.tsw_comparator: But to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus you shall say to him: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the words that you heard:

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated humbling, shifts God/me, and reciprocal hearing.
verses.before: Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before me and tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, says the LORD.
verses.after: Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and its inhabitants—because you humbled yourself before me, tore your clothes, and wept before me—I too have heard you, declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before me and tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains peace promise beside later violent death without silently resolving the tension.
verses.before: Look, I am gathering you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see all the disaster that I am bringing upon this place and its inhabitants.” They returned the word to the king.
verses.after: I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see all the disaster I am bringing on this place and its inhabitants.’” They brought this answer back to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am gathering you to your ancestors, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes shall not see all the disaster that I am bringing upon this place and its inhabitants.” They returned the word to the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps full leadership summons before the larger assembly.
verses.before: Then the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.after: The king sent word and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves male-specific first group and inclusive final assembly; law now covenant book.
verses.before: The king went up to the house of the LORD, with all the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, Levites, and all the people from great to small. He read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: The king went up to the LORD's house with all the men of Judah, Jerusalem's inhabitants, the priests and Levites, and all the people, great and small. He read in their hearing every word of the book of the covenant found in the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king went up to the house of the LORD, with all the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, Levites, and all the people from great to small. He read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains three instruction terms and total heart/soul commitment without adding a pillar.
verses.before: The king stood in his place and made the covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and with all his life, to do the words of the covenant written in this book.
verses.after: The king stood in his place and made the covenant before the LORD: to follow the LORD and keep his commands, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and all his soul, carrying out the covenant's words written in this book.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king stood in his place and made the covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and with all his life, to do the words of the covenant written in this book.

verses.rationale: Keeps king's directive and people's response, without inventing a spoken oath.
verses.before: He caused everyone who were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand to it, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.
verses.after: He made everyone present in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand with him in it. Jerusalem's inhabitants acted in accordance with the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: He caused all who were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand to it, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Preserves compelled service and lifetime qualification rather than voluntary universal conversion.
verses.before: Josiah removed all the detestable things from all the lands that belonged to the children of Israel and made everyone found in Israel serve the LORD their God. All his days they did not turn away from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
verses.after: Josiah removed all the detestable things from all the lands belonging to Israel. He made everyone present in Israel serve the LORD their God. Throughout his lifetime they did not turn away from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Josiah removed all the detestable things from all the lands that belonged to the children of Israel and made everyone found in Israel serve the LORD their God. All his days they did not turn away from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Keeps first-month date distinct from Hezekiah's second-month celebration.
verses.before: Josiah made a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.after: Josiah celebrated a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem. They slaughtered the Passover animals on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.tsw_comparator: Josiah made a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

verses.rationale: Retains assignment and encouragement as distinct royal actions.
verses.before: He appointed the priests to their duties and strengthened them for the service of the house of the LORD.
verses.after: He assigned the priests to their duties and encouraged them in the service of the LORD's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: He appointed the priests to their duties and strengthened them for the service of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follows read teaching participle, retaining unexplained ark placement and shoulder image.
verses.before: He said to the Levites who taught all Israel, who were holy to the LORD, “Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David king of Israel built. You need not carry it upon your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel.
verses.after: He told the Levites who taught all Israel and were holy to the LORD, “Put the holy ark in the house built by Solomon son of David, king of Israel. You no longer have to carry it on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to the Levites who taught all Israel, who were holy to the LORD, “Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David king of Israel built. You need not carry it upon your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps two written royal authorities and family/division organization.
verses.before: Prepare yourselves according to your ancestral houses, according to your divisions, by the writing of David king of Israel and by the writing of Solomon his son.
verses.after: Prepare yourselves by ancestral families in your divisions, following the written directions of David king of Israel and of his son Solomon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Prepare yourselves according to your ancestral houses, according to your divisions, by the writing of David king of Israel and by the writing of Solomon his son.

verses.rationale: Unfolds correspondence between lay family groups and serving Levite divisions.
verses.before: Stand in the Holy Place according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of your brothers, the people, and according to the division of a Levitical ancestral house.
verses.after: Stand in the sanctuary by the ancestral family groups of your fellow people, with a division of Levite families for each.
verses.tsw_comparator: Stand in the Holy Place according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of your brothers, the people, and according to the division of a Levitical ancestral house.

verses.rationale: Preserves imperative sequence without silently moving consecration ahead of slaughter.
verses.before: Slaughter the Passover, consecrate yourselves, and prepare for your brothers, to do according to the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses.”
verses.after: Slaughter the Passover animals, consecrate yourselves, and prepare for your fellow people, carrying out the LORD's word given through Moses.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Slaughter the Passover, consecrate yourselves, and prepare for your brothers, to do according to the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses.”

verses.rationale: Keeps donor, two totals, and Passover small livestock distinct from cattle.
verses.before: Josiah contributed to the people from the flock lambs and young goats, all for the Passover offerings for everyone who were present, thirty thousand in number, and three thousand cattle. These were from the king’s possessions.
verses.after: Josiah contributed from his own possessions thirty thousand lambs and young goats for the people's Passover offerings, for everyone present, and three thousand cattle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Josiah contributed to the people from the flock lambs and young goats, all for the Passover offerings for all who were present, thirty thousand in number, and three thousand cattle. These were from the king’s possessions.

verses.rationale: Preserves three named temple donors and two exact totals.
verses.before: His officials also contributed willingly to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, rulers of the house of God, gave to the priests for Passover offerings two thousand six hundred and three hundred cattle.
verses.after: His officials also gave freewill contributions to the people, priests, and Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, officials of God's house, gave the priests two thousand six hundred Passover animals and three hundred cattle.
verses.tsw_comparator: His officials also contributed willingly to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, rulers of the house of God, gave to the priests for Passover offerings two thousand six hundred and three hundred cattle.

verses.rationale: Follows read Cananiah consistently; retains sibling group and other three leaders.
verses.before: Conaniah and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, rulers of the Levites, contributed to the Levites five thousand Passover offerings and five hundred cattle.
verses.after: Cananiah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, along with Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, leaders of the Levites, contributed five thousand Passover animals and five hundred cattle for the Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Conaniah and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, rulers of the Levites, contributed to the Levites five thousand Passover offerings and five hundred cattle.

verses.rationale: Keeps priest stations and Levite divisions distinct.
verses.before: So the service was prepared, and the priests stood at their station and the Levites by their divisions according to the king’s command.
verses.after: The service was arranged. The priests took their places and the Levites their divisions, as the king had commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the service was prepared, and the priests stood at their station and the Levites by their divisions according to the king’s command.

verses.rationale: Supplies contextual blood and distinguishes concurrent sacrificial jobs.
verses.before: They slaughtered the Passover, and the priests threw the blood received from their hand, while the Levites skinned the animals.
verses.after: They slaughtered the Passover animals. The priests splashed the blood handed to them, while the Levites skinned the animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: They slaughtered the Passover, and the priests threw the blood received from their hand, while the Levites skinned the animals.

verses.rationale: Retains distribution for offering and the separate cattle clause.
verses.before: They removed the burnt offerings to give them according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of the people, to offer to the LORD, as written in the book of Moses. And so with the cattle.
verses.after: They set aside the burnt offerings to distribute them to the ancestral family groups of the people, to offer to the LORD as written in the book of Moses. They did the same with the cattle.
verses.tsw_comparator: They removed the burnt offerings to give them according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of the people, to offer to the LORD, as written in the book of Moses. And so with the cattle.

verses.rationale: Keeps general cook verb and fire-versus-vessels distinction rather than silently harmonizing terminology.
verses.before: They roasted the Passover with fire according to the ordinance, and they boiled the holy offerings in pots, cauldrons, and pans and quickly brought them to all the people.
verses.after: They cooked the Passover over the fire as prescribed. The sacred offerings they cooked in pots, kettles, and pans, and hurried them out to all the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: They roasted the Passover with fire according to the ordinance, and they boiled the holy offerings in pots, cauldrons, and pans and quickly brought them to all the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated preparation, Aaronic identification, and until-night duration.
verses.before: Afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night. So the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.
verses.after: Afterward they prepared food for themselves and the priests, because the priests, Aaron's descendants, were offering the burnt offerings and fat until night. So the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, Aaron's descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night. So the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

verses.rationale: Keeps all musical authorities and uninterrupted service enabled by fellow workers.
verses.before: The singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their station according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king’s seer, and the gatekeepers were at each gate. They did not need to leave their service, for their brothers the Levites prepared for them.
verses.after: The singers, Asaph's descendants, remained at their stations according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's seer. The gatekeepers stayed at every gate. They did not need to leave their service, because their fellow Levites prepared food for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their station according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king’s seer, and the gatekeepers were at each gate. They did not need to leave their service, for their brothers the Levites prepared for them.

verses.rationale: Preserves both ritual tasks and same-day organization.
verses.before: So all the service of the LORD was prepared that day to make the Passover and offer burnt offerings upon the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.
verses.after: All the LORD's service was arranged that day for celebrating the Passover and offering burnt offerings on the LORD's altar, as King Josiah commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all the service of the LORD was prepared that day to make the Passover and offer burnt offerings upon the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.

verses.rationale: Keeps Passover and seven-day festival distinct but connected.
verses.before: The children of Israel who were present made the Passover at that time and the Festival of Unleavened Bread seven days.
verses.after: The Israelites present celebrated the Passover at that time and the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel who were present made the Passover at that time and the Festival of Unleavened Bread seven days.

verses.rationale: Preserves Samuel comparison and full participating assembly rather than borrowing Kings' judges wording.
verses.before: No Passover like it had been made in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet, and none of the kings of Israel had made a Passover like what Josiah made, with the priests, Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.after: No Passover like it had been celebrated in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. None of Israel's kings had celebrated a Passover like the one Josiah celebrated with the priests, Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and Jerusalem's inhabitants.
verses.tsw_comparator: No Passover like it had been made in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet, and none of the kings of Israel had made a Passover like that which Josiah made, with the priests, Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps chronology anchored to reign year, not Josiah's age.
verses.before: In the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign this Passover was made.
verses.after: This Passover was celebrated in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign this Passover was made.

verses.rationale: Preserves restoration-to-war transition and exact place without adding the unnamed opponent.
verses.before: After all this, when Josiah had prepared the house, Neco king of Egypt went up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.
verses.after: After all this, when Josiah had put the house in order, Neco king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates. Josiah went out to meet him.
verses.tsw_comparator: After all this, when Josiah had prepared the house, Neco king of Egypt went up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult house-of-war phrase and Neco's divine claim as his speech.
verses.before: Yet Neco sent messengers to him, saying, “What have I to do with you, king of Judah? I am not coming against you this day but against the house with which I am at war, and God has commanded me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, so that he does not destroy you.”
verses.after: Neco sent messengers to him: “What is there between you and me, king of Judah? I have not come against you today, but against the house with which I am at war. God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, or he will destroy you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Neco sent messengers to him, saying, “What have I to do with you, king of Judah? I am not coming against you this day but against the house with which I am at war, and God has commanded me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, so that he does not destroy you.”

verses.rationale: Retains disguise and narrator's affirmation of divine speech through Neco.
verses.before: Yet Josiah did not turn his face from him. Instead he disguised himself to fight with him and did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God. He came to fight in the Valley of Megiddo.
verses.after: But Josiah would not turn away from him. He disguised himself to fight him and did not listen to Neco's words from God's mouth. He went to fight in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Josiah did not turn his face from him. Instead he disguised himself to fight with him and did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God. He came to fight in the Valley of Megiddo.

verses.rationale: Keeps archers and king's direct urgent request.
verses.before: The archers shot King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, “Take me away, for I am severely wounded.”
verses.after: The archers shot King Josiah. He told his servants, “Take me away. I am badly wounded.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The archers shot King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, “Take me away, for I am severely wounded.”

verses.rationale: Preserves two chariots and Jerusalem-before-death sequence without harmonizing Kings.
verses.before: His servants removed him from the chariot, put him in the second chariot that he had, and brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
verses.after: His servants moved him out of his chariot, put him in his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried in his ancestors' tombs. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned Josiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: His servants removed him from the chariot, put him in the second chariot that he had, and brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

verses.rationale: Retains female singers and documentary title without equating it to canonical Lamentations.
verses.before: Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all the male and female singers spoke about Josiah in their laments to this day. They made them an ordinance in Israel. Look, they are written in the Laments.
verses.after: Jeremiah composed a lament for Josiah. To this day all the male and female singers speak of Josiah in their laments. They made these a lasting practice in Israel, and they are written in the Laments.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all the male and female singers spoke about Josiah in their laments to this day. They made them an ordinance in Israel. Look, they are written in the Laments.

verses.rationale: Preserves loyal love and Mosaic alignment across the sentence's verse boundary.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and his steadfast deeds, according to what is written in the instruction of the LORD,
verses.after: The rest of Josiah's acts, his deeds of loyal love in keeping with what is written in the LORD's law,
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and his steadfast deeds, according to what is written in the instruction of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Closes the repeated deeds notice without deleting meaningful summary repetition.
verses.before: and his acts, first and last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.after: and his acts from first to last are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: and his acts, first and last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
